title: Persuading Domino to play Las Vegas
summary: Domino balked at six thousand dollars, but Thomas told him Vegas would set him for life; his gambling debt is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: When did he get away from the agency that you were with? How did that happen? Because he's still a big man in Vegas.
Well, the guy that bought the company, I think he made a deal with Joe Glaser to pick him up. And now Joe Glaser's office books him.

But Domino made his own... I mean, he made his own track in Vegas. Because the first time we booked him in Vegas, I had something to do with that. Whittemore... Nobody could talk Domino into taking the contract. So just off the top of my head... Well, Whittemore asked me to go and see about it, because they knew I was close to Domino. I used to hang out with him, you know. So he knew I was close to him. And he said, "Walter, see if you can get Domino to..." Because it was in his department, not in my department, because I was in the one-nighters, but he was in the clubs. So I went to Domino, and just off the top of my head I told him, I said, "Man, if you play Vegas and do good, you'll be set for life." It came just came to me, and I blurted out what I thought! And he took the deal.

The reason he didn't want to take it, they were only offering him six thousand and fifty dollars a week, and man, he was making $10,000 in a lot of the clubs all around the country! And he thought that was the best money he was making. But he hadn't played Vegas. See, Vegas is another thing, which I knew. Because I knew if he went to Vegas and did good, they'd give you twenty weeks or forty weeks a year!
Yeah. And to this day, that's where his biggest money is coming. He's getting about $20,000 a week now. The first time we went out there, we didn't know he gambled.

Man, he lost money... He didn't lose too much, I don't think, in the club he was playing. But some little club down the street, the California Club, he owed the guy $80,000 or something like that. So the record man had money in the till to pay him. So the record man went out there and paid off... Well, he paid off the $80,000, and then the club where he worked, they let him come back in there and work. They didn't really want him, he was making so much money... And the guy in Vegas... Our agent in California booked him in Vegas, and he called us and said
that the man at the club in Vegas...that he had never seen so many performers(?) in his club since he had it. But there still was Domino's fans.
And that shows you that a White person will go to a place they want to go to see somebody, but they ain't goin' to no ordinary dance hall...
